task_completion.description: The Weasis medical viewer application is open and visible on the desktop.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The Weasis application window is active, showing the medical imaging interface.

task_completion.description: A DICOM image (CT scan) is loaded into the main viewing pane of Weasis.
task_completion.visual_evidence: A cross-sectional medical image (CT) is displayed in the central viewport of the application.

task_completion.description: An arrow annotation tool has been used to point to a specific anatomical structure.
task_completion.visual_evidence: A graphical arrow is visible on top of the CT image, pointing toward a specific area.

task_completion.description: A text label with the exact string 'Suspected lesion' is placed near the arrow.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The text 'Suspected lesion' is clearly legible on the image, associated with the arrow annotation.

task_completion.description: The export or 'Save As' dialog is opened and configured for JPEG format.
task_completion.visual_evidence: An export/save dialog box is visible with 'JPEG' selected as the output format.

task_completion.description: The agent completes the export process to the specified file path.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The file browser or a terminal 'ls' command shows the file 'annotated_finding.jpg' exists in the ~/DICOM/exports/ directory.

integrity.description: The agent used the Weasis GUI tools to create annotations rather than command-line image manipulation.
integrity.visual_evidence: Screenshots show the mouse cursor interacting with the Weasis toolbar (arrow/text icons) and the image canvas.

integrity.description: The agent did not simply rename an existing image to the target filename.
integrity.visual_evidence: The trajectory shows the step-by-step process of opening Weasis, loading the DICOM, and drawing the annotations.

integrity.description: The agent interacted with the actual Weasis menus for exporting with burned-in annotations.
integrity.visual_evidence: The export settings dialog is visible, showing options like 'Drawings' or 'Annotations' being included in the export.

privileged_info_for_vlm: The exported file must be named 'annotated_finding.jpg' and located in '/home/ga/DICOM/exports/'. The text label must be exactly 'Suspected lesion'. The exported file size should be greater than 10,000 bytes to ensure it contains actual image data rather than an empty file.
